title: annualValue ignores 'quarter', so two quarterly playbooks rank at a quarter of their year
body:
## Summary
`annualValue` (apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/model.ts) scales month x12 and week x52 but not quarter, and two shipped playbooks are priced per quarter; a third hand-kept list of yearly units sits in apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:78.

## Description
The shipped `economics.per` values are year (71), episode (22), month (4), quarter (2: ifta-quarterly $1,200, grant-drawdown-reporting $2,500) and estate (1). `annualValue` (apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/model.ts, the switch under "A playbook's value on one scale") returns the raw value for quarter, so the ledger's value sort (`sortLedger`, key value) ranks ifta-quarterly at $1,200 a year instead of $4,800. Both playbooks' own basis text says "Times a year: four". Three hand-kept lists name the period vocabulary: `PER` words in model.ts (year, month, week, run, claim), `annualValue`'s cases (month, week), and `valueCell`'s `yearly` list in apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:78 (year, month, week). Adding quarter to `annualValue` alone would make `valueCell` print "$4,800 per quarter", so the fix spans both files. Fixed means one exported table (unit -> times a year) read by `annualValue` and `valueCell`, with a test that every `per` the shipped set uses is either in it or declared one-off.

## Flow
- Chores depth -> catalogue -> sort by value: ifta-quarterly sorts as $1,200 a year among yearly playbooks
- build: export PER_YEAR = { year: 1, quarter: 4, month: 12, week: 52 } from modules/playbooks/model.ts; annualValue multiplies by it
- scenes/chores/model.ts valueCell: yearly = unit in PER_YEAR
- test: for every PLAYBOOKS p, p.economics.per is in PER_YEAR or in a named one-off set (episode, estate, run, claim); ifta-quarterly annualValue = 4800 and valueCell says 'a year'

## Expected impact
A person sorting the catalogue by money sees the two quarterly chores where their yearly worth puts them. Could break: chores model tests that pin the current value cells.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one period vocabulary for the value sort and the value cell
Before: 2 of 100 shipped playbooks under-ranked 4x on the value sort; 3 hand-kept unit lists
After: predicted 0 under-ranked, 1 list (simulation on the two quarterly playbooks)
Method: simulation - walked ifta-quarterly and grant-drawdown-reporting through annualValue and valueCell; the fix needs apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/model.ts annualValue: case "month": v * 12; case "week": v * 52; default: v
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:78 const yearly = ["year", "month", "week"].includes(view.playbook.economics.per);
playbooks/*/playbook.json per counts: 71 year, 22 episode, 4 month, 2 quarter, 1 estate
playbooks/ifta-quarterly/playbook.json:78-79 "value_usd": 1200, "per": "quarter"
instrument: a model test over PLAYBOOKS: every per is a yearly unit or a declared one-off, ifta-quarterly annualValue 4800, its valueCell per 'a year'

title: The Chores depth's loading and failed states have no fixture to draw them
body:
## Summary
`PlaybooksModel` carries `loading` and `problem`, and the Chores view draws a branch for each, but no fixture in apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/fixtures.ts or apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/fixtures.ts sets either.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/view.tsx:67 draws a ProblemNote when `model.problem` is set and :74 a pending line while `model.loading`. Every module fixture is `selectPlaybooks(list, NOOP)` with the defaults loading=false, problem=null (apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/fixtures.ts, the `fixtures` record), and the Chores scene's IDS list (apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/fixtures.ts:27) reuses those. So the preview harness, the scene test that renders every fixture (apps/desktop/src/console/scenes.test.tsx:53) and any screenshot can never draw the two states a lazy load makes real. Fixed: `loading` and `failed` fixtures in the module record, listed in the Chores IDS, so `scenes.test.tsx` renders them.

## Flow
- preview.html?scene=chores&fixture=<any>: no fixture renders the loading or the failed branch
- build: fixtures.loading = selectPlaybooks([], NOOP, true); fixtures.failed = selectPlaybooks([], NOOP, false, 'the playbooks could not be read: ...')
- add both ids to scenes/chores/fixtures.ts IDS
- scenes.test.tsx then renders both; assert the failed one contains its ProblemNote title

## Expected impact
Whoever reviews the Chores depth in the harness or a screenshot sees the two states a person meets on a slow or failed load. Could break: nothing; the perf gate renders `typical` first.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the two load states become reviewable in the harness
Before: 0 of 2 load states have a fixture (17 IDS, all loading=false, problem=null)
After: predicted 2 of 2, rendered by scenes.test.tsx
Method: simulation - read every fixture constructor; the IDS list that makes a fixture reachable is apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/fixtures.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scenes.test.tsx rendering the two new fixture ids, asserting the ProblemNote title and the pending line

title: The portal 'open' action and its scene wiring have no caller in the running app
body:
## Summary
`PlaybookActions.open` (make the tab, then move to the page) is built by the hook and wired by the Chores depth, but nothing in the Chores view calls it: a chore's portals are listed by name and cannot be opened.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/index.ts builds `open: (url) => tabsCreate(url).then(() => afterOpen(url))`, and apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/live.tsx:26-33 passes `afterOpen` to move the depth to the new page; its header says "What the scene passes in is one thing: opening a portal makes the Browser tab". A grep of apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores for a call of `actions.open` finds none (`model.actions` is called for `copy` at topic.tsx:187 and `hand` at adopt/studio.tsx:234). flow.tsx:77 lists `p.apps` by name only. The panel that called `open` was deleted in the cutover (ADR 0095). So the person cannot open a portal or a cited source from a chore, and the hook's error path and the scene's page move are dead. Either a portal row becomes a link that calls `actions.open` (a capability choice), or the action, `afterOpen` and their test go.

## Flow
- Chores depth -> a chore's topic page -> the portals it spans: names only, no way to open one
- decision: wire `actions.open` to the portal and source rows, or delete `open`, `afterOpen` and hook.test's open cases

## Expected impact
Either the person can open the portal a chore names from the chore, or the code stops promising it. Could break: hook.test.tsx's two open cases, which pin the dead path.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the portal list is actionable, or the dead path is gone
Before: 0 callers of actions.open in src/scenes (grep); 2 tests pin the path
After: 1 caller per portal row, or 0 lines of the path
Method: probe - grep of every `actions.` call under apps/desktop/src/scenes; which way to go is a product call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
git grep -n "actions\.\(open\|copy\|hand\)" -- apps/desktop/src/scenes -> topic.tsx:187 model.actions.copy, adopt/studio.tsx:234 model.actions.hand; no open
apps/desktop/src/modules/playbooks/index.ts open: (url) => void tabsCreate(url).then(() => afterOpen(url)).catch(failed)
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/live.tsx:26 const afterOpen = useCallback((url) => { ... go(pagePath(origin)) }, [go]);
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/flow.tsx:77 {p.apps.map((a) => ( ... name only

title: First paint is 155 kB gz by today's build; the 125 kB budget has no byte gate
body:
## Summary
ADR 0095 and docs/redesign/parity.md say the first frame is about 125 kB gzipped and that console/graph.test.ts pins it, but the test counts files, not bytes, and a build today loads 155.4 kB gz of JS for chrome.html.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/console/graph.test.ts walks static imports and rejects named classes of file; it cannot see a module growing, a dependency added inside an allowed file, or the shared chunk filling up. A vite build of the current tree (outDir in the temp dir, manifest on) loads 12 chunks for chrome.html: app 118.3 kB gz (ADR 0095: 97), root 26.1 kB (27), and ten small ones, 155.4 kB gz in all against the recorded ~125. page-load-pipeline/field-measured-load-budget: gate first-load script bytes per route from the build being judged, and fail on absent numbers. Fixed: a script that builds with a manifest, walks chrome.html's static chunk imports, gzips them and fails over a ratchet (set at today's figure, lowered when it drops), plus a test of the script on a fixture manifest.

## Flow
- vite build --manifest -> walk manifest['chrome.html'].imports -> gzip each chunk -> 155.4 kB
- build: scripts/first-paint.mjs with a ratchet file, run by the director with the perf gates; a unit test over a fixture manifest that fails when a chunk is missing
- correct the 125 kB figure in docs/redesign/parity.md to the measured one

## Expected impact
The first-paint budget becomes a number a gate reads instead of a sentence an ADR wrote. Could break: nothing at first (the ratchet starts at today's figure).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - first-paint JS bytes are gated
Before: 155.4 kB gz across 12 chunks, gated by nothing (recorded as about 125)
After: the same figure, failing the gate on any rise past the ratchet
Method: experiment - one vite build into the temp dir and a gzip walk of the manifest (scratch script fp-bytes.mjs); the gate script belongs in apps/desktop/scripts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
build of 2026-10-16 (HEAD c097101), chrome.html static chunks, gzip kB: app 118.3, root 26.1, voice-setup 3.3, jsx-runtime 3.0, halo-signal 1.9, daemon 0.8, ProblemNote 0.5, rolldown-runtime 0.4, react 0.4, chrome 0.3, StatusDot 0.2, Badge 0.2 = 155.4
docs/adr/0095-...md: "about 125 kB gzipped to draw the first frame (the shared chunk 97 kB, the console 27 kB)"
docs/redesign/parity.md:120 "first-paint JS is about 125 kB gzipped (app 97 + console 27), pinned by console/graph.test"
instrument: a build-and-gzip script over the vite manifest with a ratchet, and its unit test on a fixture manifest
built_in: 27810da (ratchet; the 125 kB gap is a Lane C card in desktop-build-config)

title: The console reads the OS reduced-motion preference only when it happens to re-render
body:
## Summary
apps/desktop/src/console/Console.tsx:69 computes the stage's `calm` from `systemPrefersReduced()` during render, with no subscription, so turning reduced motion on while Main sits idle leaves the stage's JS on full motion until something else re-renders it.

## Description
stores/settings.ts:275 listens for the media query and rewrites `data-motion`, but nothing re-renders the console on that event: `motion` in the settings store does not change when the choice is `system`. Stage takes `calm` into every move it dispatches (apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:89) and into the Backdrop (:135). So the CSS side follows the OS at once and the JS side follows it at the next unrelated render. Whether a person sees motion in that window depends on how much of the move is JS-driven, which this round did not measure. Fixed: `calm` from a `useSyncExternalStore` over the media query (or a `systemReduced` field the settings store's listener writes), so the change re-renders the console.

## Flow
- Settings Motion = system; Main idle on a depth
- turn on Windows' 'Show animations' off (reduced motion)
- data-motion flips to calm; Console is not re-rendered, Stage still gets calm=false
- the next depth move is dispatched as a full move

## Expected impact
A person who needs reduced motion gets it from the first move after they ask for it. Could break: nothing visible when settings already re-render.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Calm follows the OS at once in the stage's JS as it does in CSS
Before: Console re-renders on 0 of 1 media-query change events (no subscriber)
After: predicted 1 of 1
Method: simulation - traced the listener (stores/settings.ts:275) and every input of Console's render; a jsdom test with a mocked matchMedia would decide it, and the stores side is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: jsdom test rendering Console (or its calm hook) with a mocked matchMedia, firing change, asserting calm=true without another store write

title: A bench with no wall time reads as '1 s' with Athena
body:
## Summary
`minutes` in apps/desktop/src/lib/playbooks.ts clamps anything under a minute up to at least "1 s", so a bench.json without `wall_s` (parsed as 0) shows Athena's time as 1 second on the topic page (apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:157).

## Description
`parseBench` reads `wall_s` leniently with a 0 default (apps/desktop/src/lib/playbooks.ts, parseBench). `minutes(0)` returns `${Math.max(1, Math.round(0))} s` = "1 s". The topic band draws `minutes(b.wallS / 60)` for any benched playbook (apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:157), so a run whose wall time is unknown is shown as a 1-second run: a measurement nobody took, which the model's header calls a lie ("a zero would be a lie"). `speedup` already refuses a zero. None of the 100 shipped benches lacks wall_s today, so this is latent. Fixed: the band shows no Athena figure (or a dash) when wallS is 0, and `minutes` is not asked to format a zero.

## Flow
- a bench.json without wall_s -> parseBench wallS 0
- topic page -> Athena's time: minutes(0) -> "1 s"
- fix in scenes/chores/model.ts: athena = b && b.wallS > 0 ? {...} : null (or figure '–'); test with a bench lacking wall_s

## Expected impact
A run with no recorded time stops claiming one second. Could break: nothing in the shipped set.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no figure is shown that was not measured
Before: parsePlaybook(raw, { verdict: {...} }) -> topic figure "1 s" (0 shipped cases)
After: no figure, or '–' (0 shipped cases)
Method: simulation - minutes(0) evaluated by reading; the site is apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/lib/playbooks.ts minutes: if (m < 1) return `${Math.max(1, Math.round(m * 60))} s`;
apps/desktop/src/lib/playbooks.ts parseBench: wallS: num(raw.wall_s)  // 0 when absent
apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/model.ts:157 athena: b ? { figure: minutes(b.wallS / 60), ... } : null
shipped: 100 of 100 bench.json carry wall_s
instrument: a chores model test with a bench lacking wall_s, asserting no '1 s' figure
